skill.name: find-the-story
skill.description: Interview someone about something that actually happened until there is a story worth telling, then write it without bolting a lesson on the end. Use when someone says they have nothing to write about, has a vague idea they cannot shape, wants to write about an experience, or asks for a personal post. Do not invent details they did not give you, and do not inflate a small thing into a parable.
skill.summary: Find a truthful story through focused questions, one concrete detail, and a concise draft.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.value_statement: Turn vague writing ideas into a specific, truthful story through focused questions. This skill identifies the strongest detail, supports a clear draft, and stops when the story ends.
actual_capabilities: Conducts an interview with one focused question at a time.
Distinguishes a complete story from a standalone anecdote.
Finds one concrete detail that makes the account specific.
Refuses to invent missing details, sharpen quotes, or rearrange events.
Drafts the story and stops after the final meaningful beat.
Uses VoiceMOAT connections for voice profiles, voice matching, and post ideas.
limitations: It cannot create a genuine story when the interview produces no real event.
It cannot verify memories, quotes, dates, or other facts independently.
It requires the writer to provide honest details and answer questions.
VoiceMOAT features require a connected Pro or Enterprise plan.

use_cases.title: Shape a Personal Post
use_cases.description: Turn a vague experience into a concise personal post with a clear before, change, and after.

use_cases.title: Develop an Interview Story
use_cases.description: Use focused questions to uncover a specific moment and detail for a newsletter or profile.

use_cases.title: Recover a Forgotten Moment
use_cases.description: Explore an ordinary memory without embellishment and decide whether it supports a story or an anecdote.

prompt_templates.title: Start With a Moment
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask me one question at a time to find a real moment worth turning into a story.

prompt_templates.title: Test the Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about this experience, then tell me whether it is a story or an anecdote.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Detail
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify one concrete detail from this event without inventing facts or improving my memory.

prompt_templates.title: Draft and Stop
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me, preserve my facts and voice, draft the story, and stop at the final meaningful beat.

output_examples.input: I want to write about a difficult project, but I only remember that it was stressful.
output_examples.output: Start with the last moment when your view of the project changed. I will ask one question at a time.

output_examples.input: The meeting was awkward, then everyone left. Nothing changed.
output_examples.output: This is an anecdote, not a full story. It may work as a short post without adding a lesson or invented turning point.

output_examples.input: I remember seeing a red error message at 11:40 p.m. and calling my teammate.
output_examples.output: The red error message and exact time provide a concrete anchor. The draft should keep those facts and avoid guessing what happened next.

best_practices: Answer one question at a time with concrete details.
Separate remembered facts from assumptions and interpretation.
Let the final beat end the draft without adding a lesson.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a complete life story in one prompt.
Do not invent details, polish uncertain quotes, or move events for effect.
Do not force a narrative arc when the material is only an anecdote.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a truthful story draft or an honest assessment that the material is only an anecdote.

faq.question: Does it write before interviewing me?
faq.answer: No. It asks focused questions first and drafts only after finding a specific detail.

faq.question: Will it fill in missing details?
faq.answer: No. It keeps uncertain details vague instead of inventing plausible events or quotes.

faq.question: Can it write in my voice?
faq.answer: It can follow the voice you provide. A connected VoiceMOAT plan can add voice profile and matching features.

faq.question: Can it turn every memory into a story?
faq.answer: No. It distinguishes stories from anecdotes and does not force a narrative arc.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Writers, professionals, editors, and creators who need a specific personal story from a vague experience can use it.
